Author: namibj
Content:
I'm gonna draw up a 2L flex board using the JLC special (5pcs up to 100x100 2L 1/3oz thin PI core only no stiffeners no soldering); I'm currently planning to do a multi-opportunity breakout board that utilizes the 3 flip chip bond pad structures in various combinations/styles (there's 3 nets; 2 of the 3 structures only have one pad per net; the third structure has larger grid pads and offers each net twice and routed so that it's at most diagonally/corner adjacent not sidways to challenge bonding processes that may be prone to shorting out adjacent pins), wiring out the DUT nets to some sort of "connector" that an ohmmeter can then be connected to for testing bond quality.
What kind of connector would you think I should go with there?
Some kinda 4-wire ZIF style replicated around the outer border to hopefully cover all the DUT bonds so that a tester could be ZIF-connected to all of them in series to try them?
Just a wider ZIF connector for like each DUT/bond site approximately and plan on using an external breakout from that to a pin header or such?
Solder connections for attaching pin headers to the flex around the edge after the flip chip bonding has been done?

Any opinions? @Essen @Lauri @Andrew Wingate ?

Author: namibj
Content:
Primary testing would be 4-wire measurements of nets through the bonds at both ends; where applicable isolation testing is also on the docket.
Where there are more than 2 pads for each net bonded out (there are 4 pads on the die for each net, but most DUT bonding sites on the test flex won't have all of them), the results from pairwise 4-wire measurements ought to reveal per-bond resistance, though possibly it might require adding a third voltage measurement wire into it, I'm not sure off the top of my head.

Author: namibj
Content:
yeah works.

I took a look at the decoder generation code and it seems `RowPreDecodersT` could be taught to handle `(address_groups[0] != 3)`, specifically, `(address_groups[0] == 4)`, for a straight forward one extra bit (so up to 1024 words), as well as an easy extension by allowing to layer another pre-decoder in front of the current pre-decoder, where the new pre-decoder would merely act on this new (optional) 4th input bit of the current pre-decoder stage.
It'd have to spread them a bit more vertically I think to not get routing congestion at the current last level decoder/page pitch, but otherwise I think it should work? And like, without having to make the row periphery wider. Unless this would not possibly fit in the limited routing channels on the left side over the input DFFs; it does look quite tight there. On further look it does appear to be mighty tight already....
Seems like it'd still be worth it though, at least with a word size notably larger than the tiny 8 bit (so that the extra decoder column of row periphery space doesn't dominate).

@Tholin How large of an SRAM would you _want_ to stick in that corner if you would get to wish anything the FlexMem compiler could support if it had sufficient demand to warrant the implementation/support effort?
